changes.comment: Send replies as native Feishu rich text instead of interactive cards. `send` now serializes the authored body as one `post` message whose `md` node carries the Markdown verbatim, so headings, tables, links, fenced code, and inline `<at user_id="...">` mentions render at the positions they were written; a body whose serialized `content` would exceed the 28 KiB budget is split into ordered messages along block, fence, table-row, line, and grapheme seams. Message create and reply now share one send primitive, and a platform refusal is rethrown as one description naming the operation, HTTP status, Feishu code, reason, and `log_id`, with the original error as its cause; a resolved nonzero business code is a failed send rather than an empty receipt. Inbound parsing resolves mentions once, into ordered `mention` parts, across text placeholders, structured `at` nodes, native post `<at user_id>`, and card `<at id>`. Inline meaning is read only where the source says the value is Markdown — a native `md` node, a card `markdown`/`lark_md` field — while plain text nodes and fields stay literal, and within Markdown a backslash escape and a matching backtick run keep their contents an example rather than a mention or an image. Native posts are read from `content_v2` when present, and a mention record the platform types as an application carries no user identity, so that occurrence reads as `@name` text; an identifier no record accounts for is carried through as the source asserted it. `im.v1.message.get` no longer sends `user_id_type`, so a bot mention reads back as the open id a reply can address. Removed the Markdown-to-card renderer and `editText` along with `renderMarkdownToCards`, `cardToContent`, `cardContentBytes`, `splitMarkdownByBytes`, `RenderedCard`, `textMessageContent`, `applyMentions`, `mentionName`, `extractPostText`, and the card element/column/cell constants; `FEISHU_CARD_CONTENT_SAFE_BYTES` is gone: one content budget now covers posts and raw cards alike, and it belongs to the package rather than to its callers, so it is not exported. `OutboundTarget` drops `mentionUserIds` and `conversationKey`. Raw `sendCard` / `editCard` and native chain-of-thought I/O are unchanged.
